en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on the All-Knowing Wisdom within the Section of Puzzling Questions.
2. The Question on the Concealed and Unconcealed Nature of the Dhamma and Vinaya “Venerable Nāgasena, this was said by the Blessed One:
‘Monks, the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata shines forth when it is unveiled, not when it is concealed.’”
Furthermore, the recitation of the Pātimokkha and the entire Vinaya Piṭaka are closed and concealed.
If, venerable Nāgasena, it were appropriate or fitting in the teaching of the Conqueror, and if it were the right time, the proclamation of the Vinaya would shine forth when opened.
For what reason?
In that regard, there is only training, restraint, discipline, the precepts of virtuous conduct, the essence of meaning, the essence of Dhamma, and the essence of liberation.
If, venerable Nāgasena, it was said by the Blessed One:

“The Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata, O monks, shines forth revealed, not concealed,” then the statement that “the recitation of the Pātimokkha and the entire Vinaya Piṭaka are hidden and concealed” must be false.

“If the recitation of the Pātimokkha and the entire Vinaya Piṭaka were concealed and hidden, then that statement of the Blessed One, ‘Monks, the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata is open and radiant, not hidden,’ would be false.
This too is a dilemma presented to you; it must be resolved by you.
“It was indeed spoken, Great King, by the Blessed One:”
“Monks, the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata shines forth revealed, not concealed.
Yet the recitation of the Pātimokkha and the entire Vinaya Piṭaka are concealed and hidden; moreover, they are not concealed for everyone, but are concealed within a boundary (*sīma*).
Great King, the Blessed One established a boundary and concealed the recitation of the Pātimokkha in three ways, following the precedent of former Tathāgatas.
The recitation of the Pātimokkha is restricted by way of lineage, restricted because of the weightiness of the Dhamma, and restricted because of the weightiness of the status of a bhikkhu.
How is the recitation of the Pātimokkha restricted by way of the lineage of the previous Tathāgatas?
This is the lineage, Great King, of all the previous Tathāgatas: namely, that the recitation of the Pātimokkha in the midst of bhikkhus is restricted to those who remain [within the order].
"Just as, Great King, the kshatriya custom of the kshatriyas operates only among kshatriyas, and this ancestral tradition of the kshatriyas is closed to others;
even so, Great King, this lineage of all former Tathāgatas—namely, the recitation of the Pātimokkha in the midst of the bhikkhus—is closed to others.
Or again, Great King, just as various guilds operate on the earth, such as..."
The Mallas, Atonas, Pabbatas, Dhammagiriya, Brahmagiriya, Naṭakas, Naccakas, Laṅghakas, Pisācas,
Maṇibhaddas, Puṇṇabaddhas, Candimasūriyas, Siridevatās, Kālidevatās, Sivās, Vasudevās, Ghanikas, Asipāsas, and Bhaddiputtas—
each such secret belongs only to those respective groups and is closed to all others.
In the same way, Great King, this lineage of all former Tathāgatas—namely, the recitation of the Pātimokkha in the midst of the Bhikkhus—is closed off from others.
Thus, by way of the lineage of the former Tathāgatas, the recitation of the Pātimokkha has been established as a boundary and kept closed.
How is it that the recitation of the Pātimokkha is established as a boundary and kept closed because of the weightiness of the Dhamma?

The Dhamma, great king, is weighty and burdensome; therein, one who acts with rightness achieves distinction, and that [distinction] reaches him through his successive practice of rightness, while it does not reach him through his successive failure to practice rightness.
Let this essential Dhamma, this excellent Dhamma, not fall into the hands of those who do not practice rightness, nor be despised, disregarded, or held in contempt by them.

"May it be despised, reviled; but let not this essential Dhamma, this excellent Dhamma, having fallen into the hands of the wicked, be looked down upon, disregarded, treated with contempt, despised, reviled, or criticized.
Thus, because of the weightiness of the Dhamma, the recitation of the Pātimokkha is kept secret by establishing a boundary.
Just as, Great King, red sandalwood— excellent, supreme, noble, of pure lineage, and of the finest quality— is despised, held in contempt, reviled, mocked,
and censured when it falls into the hands of a base person; even so, Great King, let not this essential Dhamma, this excellent Dhamma,
fall into the hands of those who act with successive misconduct, nor let this essential Dhamma, this excellent Dhamma, fall into the hands of the wicked.
"May he be known, may he be despised, may he be reviled, may he be mocked, may he be censured.
Thus, because of the weightiness of the Dhamma, the recitation of the Pātimokkha is enclosed by a boundary.
How is it that, because of the weightiness of the bhikkhu’s status, the recitation of the Pātimokkha is enclosed by a boundary?
"Great King, the state of being a bhikkhu is indeed incomparable, immeasurable, and priceless in the world; it cannot be valued, weighed, or measured by anyone.
Thinking, 'Let no one who stands in such a state of bhikkhuhood be equal to the world,' the recitation of the Pātimokkha is carried out only among the bhikkhus themselves."

“Just as, great king, in the world all the most excellent and superior goods—whether cloth or rugs, or elephants, horses, chariots, gold, silver, gems, pearls, women, and other treasures, or those who are victorious in battle and heroic—all these come to the king;

even so, great king, whatever qualities there are in the world consisting of mastery of the Sugata’s tradition, conduct, restraint, and the virtue of moral discipline, they all come to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
Thus, because of the high status of the bhikkhu’s state, the recitation of the Pātimokkha has been established as a boundary and closed off.”
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena! It is so; thus do I accept it.
This is the second question, concerning what is and is not concealed in the Dhamma and Vinaya.
